title: Baton: an open-source agentic CLI platform for reviewed, tested code
excerpt: An event-driven pipeline that takes an idea through planning, validation, design, coding, testing, review and integration, with every decision cached, budget-limited and logged with its cost.

metrics.label: Automated tests, plus static analysis and dependency checks in CI
Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenRouter models

content:
01 · Discover

The problem

Coding agents are fast, but left alone they skip planning, review and tests, and nobody can see what each step cost. Teams end up babysitting each run instead of shipping.

02 · Architect

A pipeline that runs as a state machine

Baton (the jev CLI) turns an idea into reviewed, tested, integration-ready code through planning, validation, design, coding, testing, review and integration agents. The pipeline runs as a state machine, so each stage transition and decision point triggers the next agent, and runs pause at approval states until a person signs off.

Jev’s decision engine handles agent selection, model routing, confidence evaluation and fallbacks across Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenRouter, with role-specific MCP tools and reusable skills.

03 · Build

Built to be cheap, observable and safe

  • Caching: exact-match and semantic caching reuse earlier AI responses, cutting redundant LLM calls, token use and inference cost
  • Learning: failed runs are captured and fed back so future executions improve
  • Observability: every decision and attempt is logged with its cost; per-run and per-task budget limits keep spend predictable
  • Shadow mode: new behaviour, such as semantic matching, runs in shadow first to measure agreement before it is allowed to serve
  • Isolation: work happens in Git worktrees with human approval checkpoints and auditable runs
  • Dashboard: a web dashboard on top of the CLI with conversational planning, so ideas can be talked through, queued as work and tracked live on a Kanban board

04 · Launch

Open source

Baton is open source under Apache 2.0, backed by more than 3,000 automated tests and gated by static analysis, dependency checks and GitHub Actions CI. Work arrives as reviewed, tested changes instead of raw diffs.
